anti_bias: The 4 GiB / 8 GiB decisions rest on protocol roles, planning precision, cost and structural facts (exactly-zero retention at 8 GiB), not on whether the 1.5 GiB retention effect looks strong or weak.
assumptions: 1.5/4 GiB untraced decode is bounded, not observed (see UPDATED_TIME_MODEL)
per-launch tooling overhead 1 s is an assumption
legacy-shutdown savings are a model (floor 300.8 s), not a measurement

kept_8gib.option_B_rejected: Gate 2 counters + R3-03B cost do not test the untraced P-arm timing path, so 36 launches are not redundant
why: only zero-retention falsification control for the REAL P arm: Gate 2 shows P == A == S at the counter level at 8 GiB, so P-S and P-A timing should reflect bookkeeping only
exercises the new three-arm untraced driver + helper lifecycle end-to-end at the budget where launches are cheapest
R3-03B measured S-A at 8 GiB only, never the real P arm
cheap (about 1 h central) and precise (planning half-width 2.4 ms)

primary_n.reason: N is fixed by the frozen precision rule, which does not use any retention effect; Gate 2 effect magnitude/sign was NOT used for any N decision

r3_02g_comparison.verdict: not an R3-02G-scale oversizing (~10 h, not ~64 h); the excess is confined to the 4 GiB budget, about 22% of the full wall time

scope: only the 4 GiB timing budget is unnecessary; the rest of the full design is justified

why: cannot classify R3-04 (protocol: descriptive only); protocol's own budget selection marks it droppable without changing the primary answer
planning CI half-width 14.3 ms (N=6) is ~82% of the 17.5 ms cost scale, power 0.70: the least informative contrast per machine hour (precision per hour about 1/60 of the 8 GiB control)
Gate 2 already supplies all three budgets' mechanism evidence incl. 4 GiB counters (P-A miss bytes -0.026%) and decision identity
R2-12 bridge value is historical: R2-12 is closed and 'not reinterpreted'; the future HoPi gate is its own protocol
